title: NASA announced the four crew members set to undertake the Artemis III mission so...
text:
From left, Andre Douglas, Luca Parmitano, Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio are the astronauts set to undertake the Artemis III mission.(Image: NASA via AP)

NASA announced the four crew members set to undertake the Artemis III mission soon, the next major step in the space agency's Moon Base program, meant to establish a human presence near the lunar South Pole.

The four astronauts are Randy Bresnik, Luca Parmitano, Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas and are expected to launch into Earth orbit next year. Their purpose will include testing out two commerically built lunar landers being developed to carry astronauts to the surface of the moon in 2028.

Bresnik will be the mission’s commander, with Parmitano, an Italian astronaut with the European Space Agency, serving as the pilot. Douglas and Rubio will be mission specialists, and Bob Hines will train with the crew as a backup member.

“This test flight will enable us to prove we can carry out highly choreographed operations with our partners across hardware interfaces, software propulsion systems and life support elements with crew in the high-stakes space environment,” said Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager.

All the astronaturs except Andre Douglas have been to space before. Randy Bresnik has been on two missions to the International Space Station, Parmitano served as the commander of a space station expedition in 2019, and Rubio has also been to space before.

Bresnik is a former U.S. Marine colonel, and was selected to be a NASA astronatu in 2004. He has helped develop and test spacecraft for the Artemis program as an assistant to the chief of the Astronaut Office.

Parmitano is a father of two and completed six spacewalks. Earlier, he was a test pilot for the Italian Air Force.

Rubio has served in the U.S. Army for 28 years and between 2022 to 2023, he spent 371 days on the International Space Station, breaking the record for longest-duration space flight by an American.

"My brain is going a mile a minute right now, but my heart, my heart, is so warm,” Douglas said during the NASA announcement.

The Artemis III mission is expected to last for about two weeks. “Every aspect of Artemis III will give us insight into how to refine our plans for Artemis IV,” Parsons said. “This mission is deliberately designed to take calculated risks, so that future crews will be safer and ultimately successful when we put boots on the lunar surface.”

The Artemis program, at its completion, aims to add a sustained human presence on the moon. Astronauts on Artemis III were initially supposed to land on the moon, but that plan was replaced with the agency instead focusing on increasing missions and pace of launches before a moon landing.
